probe_result: Content-addressed successor ids and durable intent records cover complementary crash-recovery gaps, while scanning immutable orphan candidates is not an authoritative recovery rule when more than one plausible child can exist. The tested safe replay rule is a write-ahead self-certifying intent capsule that binds predecessor, transition digest and stable target id before successor effects; restart reads current first, reuses the same target, and gates certificate acquisition until current==target is positively re-established. If both the trusted intent capsule and deterministic transition identity are unavailable, recovery must remain fail-closed.
neuroscience_transfer: A recurrence-sensitive latent-context renewal should behave like prospective-memory reinstatement: commit a stable intention/context token before transition, bind the successor representation to that token, and authorize reinstatement only when current-context evidence re-establishes the same token. Familiarity with one of several plausible orphan states is insufficient evidence of intended context.
mechanism_revision: Upgrade stable-target replay to a write-ahead self-certifying intent capsule. The durable recovery unit is the predecessor->intended-successor relation, not merely a successor object. Content addressing gives idempotent identity when transition material is recoverable; the intent capsule selects the intended successor among multiple durable candidates; read-current-first prevents stale-intent regression.
scope_guard: Positive result is limited to a serialized single-writer symbolic model with immutable generations, one atomic current pointer, atomic immutable intent-capsule persistence, verifiable predecessor/intent/transition digests, and fail-closed certificate gating. No claim for concurrent writers, corrupt/equivocal storage, non-atomic pointer updates, adversarial hash collisions, or the case where both intent capsule and deterministic transition identity are unavailable.

mechanism_assessment.repository_transport_role: bounded role-local persistence/readback only; no hosted compute or repository API volume used as computation
mechanism_assessment.accepted_scope: Write-ahead self-certifying intent capsule plus stable target replay prevents wrong-orphan adoption, duplicate successor allocation, stale-intent regression, and premature certificate acquisition across the six tested serialized crash-recovery cases when either trusted capsule state or deterministic transition identity remains available.
mechanism_assessment.unresolved_child: The intent capsule is now a minimal recovery root-of-trust. Its own loss, tear, corruption or stale duplication, when deterministic transition identity is also unavailable, remains unresolved and must stay fail-closed.

conflict_check: Semantic inputs were limited to the current instruction manifest/lifecycle controls, exact-blob-two-pass frozen sanitized DESIRED_STATE control26, exact-blob-two-pass frozen neuroscience config7, and own neuroscience LATEST/preflight state. No O, other-worker, downstream, legacy, shared-ledger, other-role receipt/config, scheduler, protected-primary, hosted-compute, finite-credit, paid, or manual-user execution semantics were used.
exact_next_action: Next valid invocation: test the new minimal root-of-trust itself under intent-capsule write loss, torn/corrupt capsule, and stale duplicated intent records. Compare one immutable write-ahead capsule, a two-slot append-only intent journal with monotonic predecessor binding, and generation-embedded self-certification. Require fail-closed behavior whenever a unique current intention cannot be proven; reject any scheme that infers intent solely from orphan uniqueness or requires external execution/quota-bearing recovery.
